purpose: This medicine delivers essential building blocks called amino acids — the components your body uses to make proteins — directly into your bloodstream through an IV. It is used when you cannot eat enough food by mouth or through a feeding tube to meet your body's nutritional needs. Doctors use it after surgery, during serious illness, or when your digestive system is not working properly.
how_it_works: Your body needs protein to heal wounds, fight infection, and keep muscles strong. This solution contains a carefully balanced mix of amino acids that go straight into your blood, bypassing your stomach and intestines entirely. Your body then uses these amino acids just like it would use protein from food — to build and repair tissues and keep your organs working properly.
common_side_effects: You may notice nausea, a warm or flushing feeling, headache, or mild fever. The area where the IV is inserted can sometimes become sore, red, or swollen. Your blood sugar levels may rise, which your care team will monitor closely.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease, liver disease, or any metabolic disorders, as this medicine may need to be adjusted or avoided. Blood tests will be done regularly to check your kidneys, liver, and electrolyte levels. Do not use this if the solution looks cloudy or has particles in it. It should only be given by a trained healthcare professional in a clinical setting.
typical_dosing: The dose is carefully calculated by your doctor or pharmacist based on your weight, medical condition, and nutritional needs — there is no one-size-fits-all amount. It is given slowly through an IV, often over many hours or continuously throughout the day. Your care team will adjust the rate and amount based on regular blood test results.
